ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, an iminium/imine-type fragment can be seen, with N located at the lower left and forming a double bond with the carbon on the right; near this double-bond carbon there is a circled positive charge, and it connects to a methyl group to the right. The other side of N connects to a branched carbon group. There are also curved arrows and a “:OH2” label above the figure; these are reaction annotations and are ignored according to the problem statement. Then reason: according to the left-to-right connection relationship, write it as CH3-[C+]=N-C(C)(C). The positively charged carbon is written as [C+], the C=N double bond is written as =, the branched carbon connected to N is written as C(C)(C), and the slanted stereochemical markers shown in the figure are retained, giving SMILES: C/[C+]=N/C(C)(C).

method.method_draft: First describe the drawing: the structure contains an iminium fragment with a circled positive charge on the carbon, a methyl substituent on that carbon, a double bond from that carbon to N, and an N-bound branched carbon group; the curved arrow and water label are annotations to ignore. Then translate connectivity left-to-right as CH3-[C+]=N-C(C)(C), encode the charged carbon as [C+], include the C=N double bond, add the two methyl branches on the N-bound carbon in parentheses, and preserve the depicted slash stereochemistry to obtain C/[C+]=N/C(C)(C).

With only one depicted molecule and an instruction to ignore arrows, there is no more genuinely separate reasoning path.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to identify the relevant molecular skeleton: a methyl group bonded to a positively charged iminium carbon, that carbon double-bonded to nitrogen, and the nitrogen single-bonded to a branched alkyl carbon shown as C(C)(C). Ignore the curved arrow and the :OH2 label because they are not part of the requested structure.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to determine the requested output format: provide the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure and ignore arrows/annotation marks rather than treating them as atoms or bonds.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply skeletal-structure conventions: unlabeled line ends are carbons with implicit hydrogens; explicit N is nitrogen; a circled plus at the iminium carbon is encoded as [C+]; a C=N double bond is written with '='; branches are put in parentheses; and the drawn relative geometry around the C=N bond is represented with slash stereochemical markers.
